lessons: CRITICAL fixed, exactly the defect flagged across this repo: the SHAAM allocation-number table was missing its OPENING row. It started at Jan 2025 / NIS 20,000 and omitted May 2024 / NIS 25,000 and the fact that invoices before May 2024 never needed a number. Since the skill correctly instructs the agent to scope by INVOICE issue date, a migration or catch-up run touching 2024 fell off the bottom of the table with no row to land on. Now the full table, matching the verified schedule in the sibling hashavshevet-data-tools exactly: never before May 2024, 25,000 from May 2024, 20,000 from Jan 2025, 10,000 from Jan 2026, 5,000 from Jun 2026.

CRITICAL fixed: the skill stated only ONE of the four cumulative conditions for an allocation number and then applied an unconditional buyer-side rule (do NOT debit 240, divert to a suspense account). All four are now stated: above the threshold in force on that date; the invoice carries a VAT component; the recipient is an osek murshe; and the recipient asked. Applying condition 1 alone strands deductible input VAT on B2C sales, on zero-rated and export invoices, and on pre-regime invoices. Also added the precise effect (blocks the RECIPIENT deduction, does not void the invoice) and that reverse charge is a route when a request is refused.

CRITICAL fixed: Example 3 depreciated a SERVER at 33%, the personal-computer rate. Verified directly against Tosefta Bet: mahshevim ishiyim 33, mahshevim acherim 25. A server is an other computer. The example, the rate table, the troubleshooting entry and the Hebrew mirror all said 660/month; the correct figure is 500, so the skill was overstating depreciation expense by a third every month in its only depreciation example.

REMOVED as unsourced: the 10% leasehold-improvements rate. The full appendix was fetched and enumerated and contains NO shipurim be-mushkar row at all, so a rate presented in a table headed as ITA depreciation rates was not an ITA rate. Replaced with the practice rule (shorter of lease term or useful life) and an instruction to ask for the lease term.

RATE-TABLE COMPLETENESS: furniture is 6/9/12 by venue type and vehicles are 15% only in the default M1/N1/L/O class, with taxis, driving-school vehicles, buses, rental-registered and N2/N3 classes each carrying their own higher rate. The skill had one row of each.

RATE-TABLE COMPLETENESS: the BL/health category table was missing the controlling-shareholder in a close company row (4.25 / 11.96 employee, 4.46 / 7.38 employer), which is one of the most common payroll cases in this skill own audience, and the row for a woman between her retirement age and the male retirement age (3.95 / 10.24). Both added, plus a pointer to the remaining official rows and the rule that no BL or health is charged above the 51,910 maximum insurable income.
DEAD DOMAIN removed: mas.gov.il was the sole citation behind the entire depreciation table and does not resolve (NXDOMAIN). Repointed to the regulations text.

WRONG fixed: osek patur described as simply not charging VAT. It must charge and remit VAT on a sale of real estate and on a sale of equipment where it deducted the input VAT, and certain professions cannot register as osek patur at any turnover, a list that includes bookkeeper, the skill own likely user.

WRONG fixed: Form 6111 described as for incorporated businesses. The obligation is turnover-driven and reaches self-employed oskim, with named exempt classes. PCN 874 was described as bi-monthly; it follows the osek own reporting period and has an opening record, transaction and input detail records, and a closing record.

REVIEWER DISAGREEMENT resolved by the primary source: the Expert said the working-pensioner row contradicts the domain checklist, which says the wage bears the health component only. The research pass ENUMERATED the full official BL employee table and confirmed the skill five existing rows all match it exactly, including 0% employee for a pensioner drawing an old-age pension. The skill is right and the checklist anchor is what needs correcting.

VALIDATOR: the edits pushed SKILL.md to 5,135 words, over the 5,000 cap. Moved the VAT-input-by-expense-class and OPENFORMAT/PCN874/6111 sections into references/vat-input-and-filing-formats.md with a pointer, both languages. Back to 4,821.

Deferred (Expert CRITICAL): payroll income tax is explicitly not computed and no 2026 bracket table or credit-point value is published, so the largest number in a payslip is left to the caller. Withholding at source has an account number and one Gotcha sentence but no posting rule, no rates and no example. Convalescence pay is claimed in the metadata description and appears nowhere as a payroll line. All three are domain-checklist Must-cover rows.

Deferred (Expert MAJOR): no inventory account, no COGS, no year-end close sequence despite account 830 existing and never being used, no advance tax payments (mikdamot), no foreign-currency or exchange differences, no bad-debt VAT relief, no self-invoice or import VAT, no vacation and sick accruals, and no book-retention period.

Deferred (Expert MAJOR): employer keren hishtalmut above the 15,712 ceiling is named as a taxable benefit with no posting consequence stated, so the gross-up into the income-tax and BL bases never happens. Also unstated: the 3x-employee cap on the employer keren exemption, and the 4.5% recognised-expense limit for a controlling shareholder.

Expert MINOR deferred (Phase 4.1 cap): convalescence pay (דמי הבראה) is documented as an input-driven payroll line in Step 5 but is not shown in the worked Example 1 journal entry. CRITICAL FIX: the depreciation formula read '(Cost - Accumulated depreciation) * Annual rate / 12' while the same sentence claimed straight-line and the worked example used Cost * rate / 12. That formula is reducing-balance. Following it literally understates year-2 depreciation and the accountant reverses the whole schedule. Now Cost * rate / 12 with the first-period convention stated explicitly in the example.

CRITICAL FIX, AND A REVERSAL OF LAST CYCLE: the 1.3.0 log records 'input VAT on כיבוד קל is 2/3' as a resolved fix. It was wrong. 2/3 is the vehicle-upkeep fraction (and even there the citation was wrong, it is regulation 18, not 14). My own first correction this cycle over-shot to 0% on the strength of regulation 15A. The settling evidence is Kol-Zchut's worked example: an osek murshe deducts 80% of the PRE-VAT base while an osek patur deducts 80% of the VAT-inclusive total, which only follows if the murshe reclaimed the input VAT. So routine kibud at the place of business is deductible input VAT; 15A blocks employee benefits (meals, staff events, gifts), which is now its own separate row. Two reviewers disagreed on this and neither was right on its own.

CRITICAL FIX: payroll credited net pay straight to Bank (210) on the accrual date, but Israeli salary is paid the following month. That understates the bank by a full month of net payroll and makes the bank reconciliation impossible to tie. Added account 770 salary payable, changed the accrual entry, and added the separate payment-date entry.

CRITICAL FIX: 'Asset recorded at cost (excluding VAT which is recoverable)' was stated as a general rule, but where input VAT is blocked (passenger car) the blocked VAT is part of the asset cost and must be capitalized and depreciated. As written it understated a vehicle asset and its depreciation base by 18%.

FIX: the chart of accounts was presented as 'the standard Israeli account numbering system' and the file then contradicted itself in a Gotcha claiming '1xxx = assets'. Relabeled as an illustrative convention. Note the expert pushback that 'no statutory chart' is slightly overstated: the bookkeeping directives plus the OPENFORMAT B110 record effectively force a 6111-mappable classification, so the wording now says the numbering must MAP to 6111 rather than that anything goes.

FIX: severance was a flat 8.33%. Now 'up to 8.33%' with the section 14 nuance. Two things the first draft got wrong and the expert caught: section 14 relief reaches only the portion actually DEPOSITED, so an employer depositing 6% still carries the 2.33% completion as a liability, and section 14 depends on the signed arrangement meeting the general-permit conditions, not merely on money moving. I also dropped the specific '6% extension-order floor' figure because no evidence entry supported it.

PROCESS, my own defect this cycle: I added the VAT cash-basis paragraph and the allocation-number buyer-side rule to SKILL.md ONLY. Both were missing from SKILL_HE.md, which is the primary audience. The propagation sweep I run before the panel checks CHANGED values across the folder, but it does not catch ADDED content that exists in one language and not the other. The sweep now has to include an EN/HE section-count and new-paragraph diff, not just a stale-value grep.
